maria (eng-infra): CI started failing on mac after today's image sync. lots of objc targets erroring with `module 'MyLib' not found`

ci-bot: build #6543 failed on macos-x86-64-2 (bazel)

tom (eng-platform): ugh. error snippet? quick paste will help triage

maria (eng-infra): ```
external/third_party/MyLib/module.modulemap:1:1: error: header '/usr/local/include/MyLib/MyLib.h' not found
#include <MyLib/MyLib.h>
         ^~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
1 error generated.
```

chris (eng-runtime): that looks like include/search-paths are wrong — modulemap points at system path instead of sandboxed generated headers

maria (eng-infra): yep module.modulemap is generated by our objc_genrule, but compiler is resolving imports from /usr/local first on macos image

alan (eng-sre): new image bumped Xcode and changed default include order, likely the culprit. did we change any toolchain flags?

maria (eng-infra): not in BUILD files. this started right after infra rolled linux+mac images at 09:12. linux ok, only mac builders failing

tom (eng-platform): can you try a quick `bazel build` locally with the new image env or run a hermetic builder with the previous image? need to narrow to image vs BUILD change

maria (eng-infra): ran a local dockerized mac env (emulated) and reproduced. bisect suggests failure introduced by image roll.

chris (eng-runtime): quick mitigation: modify objc_library to set `module_map = "//path:module.modulemap"` so the compile uses the right modulemap location. small BUILD change, low risk.

maria (eng-infra): I can open a tiny PR with that BUILD tweak, but we should also file infra ticket to pin or revert image.

tom (eng-platform): please open PR and tag me. also @alan can you schedule a narrow rollback window or spin-up a staging pool with previous image for bisect?

alan (eng-sre): will do. scheduling a rollback test on a handful of builders. also adding an image-compat test to detect this class of failure early.

maria (eng-infra): created PR #7891 with module_map patch, small change, marked as revert-once-image-fixed. request review from @tom @chris

ci-bot: PR #7891: CI started (linux, mac)

maria (eng-infra): update: linux checks green, mac workers still fail with same module not found

chris (eng-runtime): ok, that means BUILD patch didn't help on mac — maybe compiler is ignoring local module_map because of search-order. can you share full clang compile command from the failed action?

maria (eng-infra): from action log: 
```
clang -c -isysroot /Applications/Xcode.app/Contents/Developer/Platforms/MacOSX.platform/Developer/SDKs/MacOSX.sdk -I/usr/local/include -I<sandbox>/execroot/..../generated_headers -fmodules -fmodules-cache-path=... -fmodule-map-file=external/third_party/MyLib/module.modulemap 
```

chris (eng-runtime): I see `-I/usr/local/include` before our generated header path. that's the problem. new Xcode image may add a default include which gets precedence. we can force order by adding `-I` before those or pass `-nostdinc` variants, but bazel flags make that annoying.

alan (eng-sre): I'm starting a staging rollback now, will run the same action on the old image to confirm. give me ~15m.

maria (eng-infra): thanks. in parallel I'll try a runtime fix: set `objc_compile` toolchain override to inject `-I<path>` earlier via `copts` for affected targets, then re-run mac CI. small, targeted.

chris (eng-runtime): if you add `copts = ["-I$(GENDIR)/.../generated_headers"]` to the objc_library that should win. ugly but workable until infra fixes image.

maria (eng-infra): pushed branch with `copts` change and kicked CI. PR #7892 now.

ci-bot: manual rerun requested by @tom: mac-legacy-image-confirmation queued

alan (eng-sre): rollback pool run complete: action succeeded on old image. confirmed regression introduced by image roll at 2025-11-02 09:12:03 UTC. filing INFRA-6327.

maria (eng-infra): great — we'll keep the temporary `copts` patch as a bandaid. will also add a follow-up TODO to remove when INFRA-6327 resolved.

tom (eng-platform): thanks team. small follow-ups: 1) add a CI smoke that builds a few objc module-based targets after image updates, 2) keep PRs small so revert is easy. :thumbsup:

chris (eng-runtime): agreed. also let's add an automated checker that flags modulemap files referencing absolute system paths — that would have caught this earlier.

maria (eng-infra): noted, filing ENG-1170 for modulemap linter. will ping when PRs are up.

alan (eng-sre): INFRA-6327 opened, rolling back image from staging to prod will happen after validation window.

maria (eng-infra): thanks all, closing triage for now. reopening if mac CI still red after fixes. :pray:
